name: 陳彥安
objective:
This course takes a modular approach to explore core research directions in modern computer vision, covering visual recognition foundations, object detection and dense prediction, vision-language and generative models, representation learning and practical challenges, and real-world vision systems. Each module spans 2–3 weeks to allow students to genuinely engage with the problem context rather than survey topics at a surface level.

The course is conducted entirely in English (EMI). Through lectures, guided paper reading, model experiments, and a final research project, students develop the ability to read papers, design experiments, and propose research directions relevant to ECE applications including edge computing, smart manufacturing, and AIoT perception.
schedule:
Week Topic
1 Course Overview and Project Guidelines
2 CNN and Transfer Learning
3 Vision Transformers
4 Object Detection I: Two-stage Methods
5 Object Detection II: One-stage, DETR, Open-vocabulary
6 Dense Prediction I: Semantic and Instance Segmentation
7 Dense Prediction II: SAM and Open-vocabulary Segmentation
8 Midterm Project Proposal
9 VLM I: CLIP and Image-Text Representation
10 VLM II: Prompting, Multimodal Reasoning, VLM Applications
11 Generative Vision: Diffusion and Synthetic Data
12 Representation Learning and Self-supervised Learning
13 Practical Issues I: Data Imbalance, Small Data, Weak Supervision
14 Practical Issues II: Robustness, Occlusion, Domain Adaptation
15 Real-world Vision Systems: Edge, Manufacturing, Robot Vision
16 Project Progress Discussion / Technical Clinic
17 Flexible Learning (Final Project)
18 Flexible Learning (Final Project)
scorePolicy:
Assignment 1: Classification / Transfer Learning 15%
Assignment 2: Detection or Segmentation 15%
Assignment 3: VLM / CLIP / Generative Vision 15%
Midterm Project Proposal 15%
Final Project (presentation + written report) 35%
Participation 5%
